caption: The drawing features a stylized depiction of a human figure on a cross, representing a crucifixion scene. The cross itself is rendered in black and gray, with horizontal and vertical beams intersecting behind the figure. The ends of the horizontal beam are decorated with blocks of color: red, cream, and black, and include symbols or letters in black and red. The human figure is predominantly light brown with red and black outlines and details accentuating muscles, wounds, and facial features. The figure's cheeks, chest, arms, and legs have distinct red markings and patterns. The head is adorned with a crown of black thorns and red, white, and yellow shapes arranged as points behind the head. The figure wears a yellow garment around the waist, decorated with a central circular pattern in red, white, and black. The legs and arms are extended, and larger stylized red wounds or marks are present on the knees, hands, and other parts of the body. The background is plain and uncolored, and the number "27" appears in small print in the bottom left corner.
title: Plate 27: Christ Crucified, Mora: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
